text:
Jenna (customer): Hey team — we're seeing our users get partial streaming responses then the client shows connection closed. Happens across Chrome and mobile web. We tried reconnect but they only get a short prefix, then no more tokens. Billing shows usage spikes.

Priya Patel: Thanks Jenna. Does the client reconnect automatically? Any error code in browser console or server logs?

Jenna (customer): Client uses EventSource with default reconnection. Console shows 'EventSource failed' then 'reconnecting in 3000ms'. No 4xx/5xx returned to client. On our side we see HTTP 200 open then after ~60s the connection resets.

Marco Li: Two quick suspects: upstream ALB/NGINX idle timeouts dropping the socket, or an intermediary proxy turning idle SSE into closed connection. Also token expiry during long streams can trigger server-side close. Can you capture raw network frames or server access logs for the exact disconnect?

Jenna (customer): Pasted the access log snippet: 

```
GET /v1/stream?model=gpt-x 200 - 00:00:00 60
499 via 10.0.0.5: upstream terminated connection
```

Priya Patel: That 499 (client closed) in nginx suggests the client closed or the proxy killed it. But since browser shows reconnect, could be ALB performing TCP idle timeout then client reconnects and gets partial content. Which client library are you using? Vanilla EventSource or polyfill?

Jenna (customer): Vanilla EventSource with a small wrapper that parses SSE events. We send keep-alive comments from server as `: ping\n\n` every 15s.

Alex G.: Good that you have comment pings. A couple of things to check: some proxies (AWS ALB) consider an HTTP connection idle if no bytes flow for their configured idle timeout, even if TCP keepalive is enabled. Make sure your keep-alive comments are actually flushed as bytes (no server-side buffering). Also verify response headers like `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and that `Content-Length` is absent.

Marco Li: Repro steps I use locally: run a simple SSE server that sends comment pings every 30s, put an nginx reverse proxy with `proxy_read_timeout 60s` and an ALB with 60s idle timeout. Then watch client drop at 60s unless a non-empty chunk is sent within that window. Comments (single ':\n') are sometimes stripped by proxies. Try sending a small data event like `event: keepalive\n` `data: .\n\n` which guarantees bytes and isn't treated as comment by some infra.

Priya Patel: Also check TLS session renegotiation on the load balancer; if TLS teardown happens, browser may not be able to continue streaming and will reconnect cleanly which looks like partial output.

Jenna (customer): We can try switching to `event: keepalive`. Any config we should change on nginx/ALB?

Alex G.: On nginx, set `proxy_buffering off; proxy_cache off; proxy_read_timeout 3600s;` and `chunked_transfer_encoding on;` if available. For ALB, increase idle timeout to > keepalive interval or send non-empty chunks more frequently than idle timeout. If you can't change ALB, use a 15s keepalive data frame.

Marco Li: One more gotcha: some HTTP intermediaries treat a stream that sends only comments or CRLF as idle. Use a single byte of data as a keepalive payload. Example SSE fragment to send every 20s:

```
event: keepalive
id: <last-event-id>
data: .

```

This also lets you correlate `last-event-id` on reconnect. Browser will set `Last-Event-ID` header on the next connection if you send `id:` fields. That helps resume logic.

Jenna (customer): Our server doesn't echo id currently. How would resume look server-side?

Priya Patel: Two simple approaches: 
- Stateless: Have the client send a request-id or last-token-index in the query param/headers when reconnecting; server replays from that offset or dedups tokens.
- Stateful: Keep a short-lived buffer in server or cache (Redis) keyed by session id to resume from last token.

Marco Li: For immediate mitigation, send `id:` on every event with the latest token index and instruct client to include `Last-Event-ID` header when reconnecting. Also add jitter and exponential backoff on reconnect attempts to avoid sudden bursts that look like traffic spikes (billing concerns).

Jenna (customer): We saw billing spikes because each reconnect started a new generate request and tokens were duplicated. Any recommended dedupe strategy?

Alex G.: Accept duplicate tokens in the short term and dedupe on client by ignoring tokens whose token index <= last-index seen. Server-side, you can accept an idempotency key (X-Request-ID) so repeated reconnects with same key will resume instead of recharging. If that's not possible, at least correlate usage in billing to avoid charging duplicates until you have a fix. I'll escalate billing exception if you provide request-ids for affected calls.

Priya Patel: Commands you can run to repro locally (curl SSE):

```
curl -v -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=test" \
  --header "Authorization: Bearer <token>"
```

Look for periodic `:` or `event: keepalive` chunks. If curl returns `Connection reset by peer` at same time your proxy idle timeout triggers, you'll hit the same issue.

Jenna (customer): Trying change to `event: keepalive` + id fields now. Also enabling `proxy_read_timeout 120s` in nginx. Will report back.

SREBot: Note created: support/INC-2026-0042 - Investigate SSE disconnects / ALB timeouts for JennaCorp. Assigned to Priya.

Priya Patel: Follow-ups I'll do: 1) Check our hosted API fronting infra for strict `comment-only` passthrough issues (some layers may strip colon lines). 2) Confirm `Last-Event-ID` handling in our gateway and whether we can accept client resume tokens. 3) Coordinate billing hold until we confirm duplicate-charge window.

Marco Li: If you still see disconnects after payload keepalives and proxy timeout tuned, capture a tcpdump on the server side around disconnect time and share. Also check client-side network panel for `Last-Event-ID` header being sent.

Jenna (customer): Thanks — switching keepalive, enabling id, will test and post logs here. Appreciate the quick turnaround. :thumbsup:

SupportBot: Tip: sending a single byte `data: \u200B` (zero-width space) also works as a no-op payload that flows through buffers if you can't change semantics.

Alex G.: One last note on timeouts vs TCP keepalive: TCP keepalive operates at the socket-level and intervals are usually >> few minutes by default. Application-level SSE pings (every 15-30s) are the reliable cross-proxy solution.

Jenna (customer): Update: After switching to `event: keepalive` every 20s and enabling `proxy_read_timeout 180`, the stream stayed up for 10+ minutes in my testing and no duplicate billing so far. Will keep monitoring.

Priya Patel: Great — we'll leave INC open for a couple days while you monitor. If any more anomalies, capture server logs and packet traces and drop them here.

Marco Li: Filing a short runbook based on this thread for support->sse keepalive guidance. I'll include examples and nginx/ALB settings.

Jenna (customer): Thanks all!
